thread:
Anna: heads-up: scheduling a short maintenance window for the east GPU pool (region: us-east2) tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. goal: soft reboots for a subset of racks + NIC microcode bump + preheat KV/prefix cache. will do staggered cohorts, canary first.
Liam: ack. what's the canary size?
Anna: canary = 2 racks (~8 GPUs). if canary looks good we'll roll cohorts of 5 racks every 10m.
Rachel: any expected throughput hit for Hosted API customers? SLA targets?
Anna: targeting <5% p95 latency impact. we'll route traffic to dedicated burst pools + fallbacks. per-route rate limiting unchanged.
Tanja: NIC microcode needs bmc soft-flash on some blades — that can cause short NIC flap during reboot. planning 3min drain per node.
Liam: do we have capacity to absorb 3min nodal drains without queue growth?
Rachel: we budgeted spare capacity earlier today, @cost-team flagged ~12% spot backfill available. should be enough for the first cohorts, but if eviction happens we need to pause.
Anna: plan: 1) canary racks drain 2) preheat KV cache (seed recent session prefixes) 3) apply microcode + soft reboot 4) monitor KV hit, p50/p95, errors 5) continue cohorts. rollback: reprovision and uncordon if errors >5% or error budget breached.
Liam: can you paste the drain commands and the exact metrics we watch?
Anna: drain snippet: ```bash
kubectl drain node/$NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
sleep 10 # verify pods rescheduled
```
Anna: watch list: `hosted-api-p95`, `inference-queue-length`, `kv-cache-hitratio`, `router-errors-per-min`. alert thresholds: p95 +200ms, queue length >1000, kv-hit <65%.
Tanja: network note: when NIC flashes we sometimes see transient ARP storms. we'll pre-warm ARP and run `bridge fdb` clear on the leaf if needed.
Rachel: how do we notify Dedicated customers? any opt-outs?
Anna: we pushed a scheduled maintenance email to customers with > SLA commitments. Dedicated customers with reserved windows get calendar invite and a support contact stack.
Liam: cost question: will rolling cohorts incur extra on-demand usage?
Rachel: small bump for warm backfill (~2-6% extra GPU minutes for the window). we can source from committed reserved pools first.
Anna: deploy-bot will post start/end and per-cohort status. I will run the canary at 02:05 UTC.
deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance posted: us-east2 east-gpu-pool maintenance starting 02:00 UTC. Canaries at 02:05 UTC. See runbook: https://internal.redwood/ops/runbooks/east-gpu-maintenance
Liam: if canary fails, is the rollback fast?
Anna: yes — uncordon + restart scheduling; KV seeding is idempotent. restore traffic routing within ~6 minutes.
Tanja: I'll be on the network watch channel and will pre-seed ARP entries 5m before each cohort.
Rachel: SRE oncall (me) will monitor alerts and open an incident if error budget exceeded.
Liam: one more: will model-value bundles need warming (LLM KV cache) after soft reboots?
Anna: yes — we'll run `kv-warm` job: ```python
# pseudo
for prefix in TOP_PROMPT_PREFIXES:
  send_dummy_requests(prefix, weight=0.7)
```
Anna: expected time to warm per cohort ~4m. that's accounted in the 10m cadence.
Rachel: thanks — add a note to the console dashboard (maintenance badge) so support sees it.
Anna: done. I'll post a checklist before 01:45 UTC and call the go/no-go at 01:55 UTC.
Liam: +1. I'll coordinate rollback scripts and make them one-liners.
Tanja: standing by. ping me for ARP/leaf clears. :thumbsup:
Rachel: If anyone wants to join the watch call, 01:50 UTC on Zoom.
Anna: thanks team. will post updates here during the window.
deploy-bot: Maintenance started: canary cohort at 02:05 UTC. status: draining nodes.
Anna: canary result: stable after preheat, p95 +50ms, kv-hit 82%. proceeding to cohort 1 at 02:18 UTC.
Liam: cohort 1 started. running `kv-warm` now.
Tanja: saw 90s NIC flap on node rack-12b, ARP pre-seed helped, no packet loss detected at downstream.
Rachel: monitoring: queue length flat, errors nominal.
Anna: cohort 1 complete. moving to cohort 2.
Liam: cohort 2 rollback triggered — one node failed to remount local SSD, pods in crashloop.
Anna: pausing rollouts. uncordon and reprovisioning node, will spin up replacement from reserved pool.
Rachel: opened incident INC-2026-045: node reprovision fail during maintenance. oncall investigating.
Tanja: network unaffected. preparing to assist for node reprovision.
Anna: replacement node up, traffic rebalanced, errors cleared. will re-evaluate cadence before continuing.
deploy-bot: Maintenance paused at 02:57 UTC for investigation.
Liam: recommendation: increase per-cohort cooldown to 20m and reduce cohort size to 3 racks.
Anna: agreed. updating runbook and notifying support. reschedule resume at 03:20 UTC if no further issues.
Rachel: I'll notify CSMs for any customer-facing impact and log cost delta once final.
Anna: thanks — follow-ups: update console banner, attach incident notes, and post final postmortem if needed.
Liam: noted. everyone stay on-call until we confirm resume or rollback complete.
Anna: thank you all.
